results.content:
## First time drawback filer?

Please go to the following link for more information: First Time Drawback Filer.

## I submitted my claim without both HTS numbers. What do I do now?

As noted in CSMS Message 19-000050, filers are required to provide the Chapter 99 HTSUS tariff number related to Section 301 and/or 201 duties, and the associated Chapter 1 to 97 HTSUS tariff number on ALL claims. [...] ## What do I do if I have a substitution claim and Section 301/201 duties?

As noted in CSMS Message 19-000050 Pre-TFTEA Substitution Claims: 301/201 duties are refundable, in full, on pre-TFTEA substitution claims. [...] If any drawback claim subject to Section 301 and/or 201 duties was previously filed and accepted in ACE, the filers are required to “perfect” the claim.  To “perfect” a claim, filers must contact their Drawback Specialist and request the claim be returned to trade control.

## 

As noted in CSMS Message 19-000050, filers are required to provide the Chapter 99 HTSUS tariff number related to Section 301 and/or 201 duties, and the associated Chapter 1 to 97 HTSUS tariff number on ALL claims. [...] ## 

As noted in CSMS Message 19-000050 Pre-TFTEA Substitution Claims: 301/201 duties are refundable, in full, on pre-TFTEA substitution claims.

TFTEA Substitution Claims: 301/201 duties are refundable on TFTEA substitution claims, even if subject to the TFTEA lesser of [value] rule.  If subject to the TFTEA lesser of [value] rule, the amount will be limited by the value of the substituted merchandise when it is lower than the value of the imported merchandise.

## [...] ## 

Just like any other drawback claim, all import entries must be liquidated, past the 180-day protest period, drawback specialist’s review must be complete, all required documents are presented and verified, there are no open protests on any imports and all refund/recon issues are resolved in order to receive a drawback refund.

results.title: U.S. Australia Free Trade Agreement Frequently Asked Questions | U.S. Customs and Border Protection
results.content:
Some tariff items do not have product-specific rules of origin because the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS) has been modified and the U.S.-Australia FTA product specific rules of origin have not yet been updated to account for these changes. If the good in question corresponds to a tariff item without a product-specific rule, the origination analysis should be performed using the most recent HTSUS that has an alternate tariff item for that good and its corresponding [...] An AUFTA claim is made by prefacing the tariff item on the entry summary with the Special Program Indicator "AU" (19 CFR 10.723) or as a post-importation claim via a Post Entry Amendment (PEA) or a Post Summary Correction (PSC).

## May a post-importation preference claim be made using 19 USC 1520(d)?

No, 19 USC 1520(d) is not an option.

## What responsibilities does an importer assume by making an AUFTA preference claim? [...] The de minimis provision allows a good to originate, as long as all non-originating materials that do not meet the prescribed tariff shift are not more than 10 percent of the adjusted value of the good (for non-textiles). However, if the good must meet a regional value content requirement to originate, the value of such non-originating materials must be taken into account when calculating the regional value content (General Note 28(g) and 19 CFR 10.732).

results.title: Section 301 Trade Remedies Frequently Asked Questions | U.S. Customs and Border Protection
results.content:
## Due to Port congestion delays, goods subject to Section 301 were not entered until after the effective date of the tariff increase. Can CBP grant relief by calling the entry timely?

Under 19 C.F.R. 141.68(e), merchandise will not be authorized for release, nor will an entry or an entry summary which serves as both the entry and entry summary be considered filed or presented, until the merchandise has arrived within the port limits with the intent to unlade. results.title: Automated Export System Frequently Asked Questions (AES) | U.S. Customs and Border Protection
results.content: No, both Schedule B and the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) numbers are acceptable for reporting export shipments in AES. Please note that there are a few exceptions when the reporting of HTS numbers as export classifications are not allowed. These exceptions are presented in the front of the HTS as well as in the AESTIR "Appendix V HTS Numbers that Cannot be Reported in AES". Schedule B numbers cannot be reported in lieu of the import HTS number when reporting import shipments. [...] ## Is the Schedule B export commodity classification system being eliminated?
